whenToUse: People need to remember a position in a list and come back to it, such as search results or order history.
People should know the total amount.
People need to reach the footer or content below the list.
whenNotToUse: Content is browsed without breaks, like a feed (consider infinite scroll).
There are only one or two pages of items.
People would have to press small number buttons repeatedly on mobile (consider a load more button).
accessibility: Wrap it in <nav aria-label> so it's announced as page navigation.
Set aria-current="page" on the current page button.
Give icon-only previous and next buttons an aria-label, and disable them at the ends.
Hide the ellipsis (…) with aria-hidden to avoid needless reading.
